## 1. Search Console metrics

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Impressions | 70 |
| Clicks | 0 |
| CTR | 0.0% |
| Average position | 13.73 |
| Expected CTR at this position | ~1.6% |
| CTR gap factor | 1.00 (maximum) |

**Volume caveat:** at 70 impressions, a "healthy" CTR of 1.6% is ~1 click.
Zero clicks is consistent with both a snippet problem and plain noise — CTR
movement on this page alone will not be statistically detectable after one
recrawl. Impressions and average position carry the measurable signal.

## 3. Editorial Completeness — 70%

Missing required elements (pillar standard):

| Missing element | Standard requires | Current state |
|---|---|---|
| Sources | `<SourcesList>` — cited primary sources | none (`hasSources: false`) |
| Internal links | 8+ in-content links out | 6 outbound |
| Comparison table | `<table>` — 2+ columns, 3+ rows | 0 tables |

Present: AI Summary (`<SummaryBlock>`), FAQ (3 Q&As + FAQPage schema), author
byline, breadcrumbs, CTA, full schema stack (Article, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage,
Person, Organization, ImageObject).

The three gaps are cluster-wide: the medigap cluster sits at 25% coverage on
Sources, Internal links, and Comparison table — whatever pattern fixes them
here is reusable across the other three cluster pages.

Cluster average: 704 words (855 excluding the pillar itself). The pillar is
the **shortest page in its own cluster at 249 words — 3.5× below the sibling
average** — yet outranks every sibling. It earns its position 13.7 on
inbound authority and structure, not content. That is the depth headroom.

Current `<title>`: `Medigap (Medicare Supplement) in Vernal, Utah | Vernal Medicare`
Current meta description: `Compare Medigap plans in Vernal and the Uintah Basin. Local, licensed help choosing a Medicare Supplement that fits your doctors and budget.`

## 7. Optimization Hypothesis

> **We expect this change to improve average position because the pillar
> already ranks at 13.7 in the striking-distance band while being 3.5× thinner
> than its cluster siblings, so adding the standard comparison table,
> definitions, sources, and 8+ internal links supplies the depth that is the
> page's only structural deficit.**

Primary metric: **average position** (secondary: impressions). CTR is
explicitly *not* the primary metric despite the queue's title/meta suggestion:
at 70 impressions, expected clicks ≈ 1, so a CTR delta cannot be attributed to
any change after one recrawl. The title/meta rewrite should still ship with
the edit, but it is evaluated later, once impressions volume matures.

Copy this hypothesis into `docs/seo/WORK-LOG.md` as a new entry **when the
edit begins** — not before.
